Bug_Title: Regex boundaries should not be used in a way that can never be matched
Bug_Details:
In regular expressions the boundaries ^ and \A can only match at the beginning of the input (or, in case of ^ in combination with the MULTILINE flag, the beginning of the line) and $ , \Z and \z only at the end.
These patterns can be misused, by accidentally switching ^ and $ for example, to create a pattern that can never
match.
Noncompliant code example
// This can never match because $ and ^ have been switched around
Pattern.compile("$[a-z]+^"); // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
Pattern.compile("^[a-z]+$");
Bug_Explanation: The regex pattern '$[a-z]+^' is formed by switching the '$' and '^' characters, which makes the pattern unable to match anything. The '$' character is used to match the end of the string, '^' is used to match the start of the string. Switching them makes the whole pattern unable to match anything.
